judge verdict.failure: The brief states 'five names -- GOOGL, META, MSFT, GEV and STX -- between 22 and 23 days out' but the data shows STX reports at 22 days while the other four report at 23 days, so STX should be listed separately before the 23-day group.

snapshot_next_report.first_output:
The hardline drives split your watchlist today. AI compute pushed higher as a group -- TSM, NVDA and AVGO all up between 2% and 3% together -- while AMD dropped 0.2%, lagging its peers by more than two and a half points. In memory and storage, WDC and STX surged 5.6% and 4.6% respectively, each outpacing the rest of the theme by around five points, while SNDK and MU both slipped under 1%. Mega-cap tech mostly rose together, though AAPL fell 0.3% while the others gained. CEG stood out from the power and infrastructure names with a 4.1% jump, well ahead of its peers.

The common thread across those divergences isn't clear from the price action alone. The moves align with overnight tech strength -- the Nasdaq 100 led with a 0.9% gain -- but whether something sector-specific drove the variance in each theme or these are company stories isn't evident from today's data.

Off your watchlist, several Brazilian fintech names jumped sharply: XP, INTR, STNE and PAGS all rose over 20%. PTC climbed 34%, also landing on the most-actives list.

TSM reports in 10 days. After that, TSLA and VRT both report in 16 days, then five names -- GOOGL, META, MSFT, GEV and STX -- between 22 and 23 days out.

failed_runs.brief:
The AI compute theme drove today's watchlist, with TSM, NVDA and AVGO all up around 2% alongside their peers. AMD broke from that pattern, finishing flat while the rest of the group rallied -- a nearly 3-point divergence that stands out in an otherwise coherent move across the theme.

Memory and storage split sharply. WDC gained 5.6% and STX rose 4.6%, each running well ahead of their peers, while SNDK and MU both slipped, falling roughly 5 points behind. The hard drive names moved together; the memory names moved together; the two groups went opposite directions. Mega-cap tech lifted broadly, most names up 1% to 2%, with AAPL the outlier, down slightly while the rest advanced. CEG jumped 4.1% in the power and infrastructure theme, pulling away from the rest of that group, which sat near flat.

Beyond the watchlist, Brazilian fintech names dominated the gainers -- XP up 32%, STNE and INTR each up over 20% -- alongside PTC, which rose 34% on the day. Those moves were large enough to land multiple names on both the active and gainer screens.

TSM reports in 10 days. TSLA and VRT follow in 16 days, then a cluster arrives late in the month: STX in 22 days, then GOOGL, META, MSFT, GEV on the same day in 23 days, with AAPL, AMZN and SNDK one day after that.
